question: What is the primary function of the microscopic microvilli lining the proximal convoluted tubule?

options.A: To increase surface area for reabsorbing substances
options.B: To push urine upward toward the renal cortex
options.C: To trap large red blood cells before filtration
options.D: To secrete excess white blood cells into the filtrate

explanation: Microvilli create a brush border that greatly expands the surface area available to pull water and nutrients back into the blood. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why is the patient's level of consciousness checked when assessing systemic circulation?

options.A: Alertness proves that heart valves are closing correctly
options.B: Consciousness measures how much glucose is stored in the liver
options.C: Mental status directly controls blood vessel width in the legs
options.D: The brain is very sensitive to drops in blood flow and oxygen

explanation: The brain requires a constant supply of oxygenated blood, making confusion or sleepiness an early warning sign of poor perfusion. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h7)

question: What is a major advantage of using topical NSAIDs instead of oral NSAIDs for older adults with osteoarthritis?

options.A: They never require a prescription from a doctor
options.B: They work within seconds to stop all joint swelling
options.C: They completely reverse the loss of joint cartilage
options.D: They have fewer systemic side effects like stomach ulcers

explanation: Topical NSAIDs deliver medicine directly to the painful joint through the skin, avoiding the high bloodstream concentrations that cause gastrointestinal bleeding. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h5)

question: Why do nurses and doctors use a special dye (contrast medium) during an IVP test?

options.A: To make the urinary tract structures visible on X-ray images
options.B: To numb the internal tissues and prevent pain during the scan
options.C: To speed up the filtration rate of the glomerulus temporarily
options.D: To flush out dangerous bacteria residing in the renal pelvis

explanation: Think of the dye as a highlighter! It travels to the kidneys and helps the drainage pathways show up clearly on the X-ray films.

question: Which antiseptic needs to dry on the skin so it can slowly release free iodine to kill germs?

options.A: Hexachlorophene
options.B: Chlorhexidine gluconate
options.C: Povidone-iodine
options.D: Isopropyl alcohol

explanation: Povidone-iodine needs a little drying time to work its magic and release free iodine onto your skin.

question: Which symptom is most characteristic of a localized infection following suture removal?

options.A: Mild itching around the adhesive strips
options.B: Temporary skin numbness near the cut
options.C: Pus drainage and spreading skin warmth
options.D: Fading pink color of the scar line

explanation: Pus and warmth indicate bacterial multiplication and active inflammation, which signal that the wound is becoming infected. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h7)

question: Which skill became essential for nurses as critical care established itself as a distinct specialty?

options.A: Managing hospital financial budgets and payroll for nursing units
options.B: Performing major abdominal surgeries independently in an emergency
options.C: Interpreting complex hemodynamic parameters and monitor waveforms
options.D: Conducting long-term outpatient psychiatric counseling sessions

explanation: Specialized nurses learned to read intricate data from monitors to catch subtle signs of patient deterioration early. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why is pushing an endotracheal tube 'blindly' dangerous in severe upper airway trauma?

options.A: It causes sudden high blood pressure.
options.B: It can worsen a tear and completely block the airway.
options.C: It stops intravenous fluids from working.
options.D: It permanently paralyzes the vocal cords.

explanation: Exactly right! Forcing a tube past swollen and damaged tissues can easily push through an existing tear, completely losing the airway.

question: Why is it important to report near-misses even though no patient was actually harmed?

options.A: To give the nursing supervisor extra paperwork to file away
options.B: To punish the staff member who almost made the mistake
options.C: To help identify hidden system weaknesses before a real injury happens
options.D: To increase the financial billing charges for the patient

explanation: Analyzing near-misses uncovers dangerous process flaws, allowing the hospital to fix them before a patient suffers actual harm. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h8)

question: Why does a baby with Tetralogy of Fallot sometimes turn very blue when crying?

options.A: The lungs suddenly fill with large amounts of clear fluid.
options.B: Deoxygenated blood mixes and enters the systemic circulation.
options.C: The heart stops beating completely for several minutes.
options.D: Blood flow to the brain increases too quickly.

explanation: Because of the heart defects in Tetralogy of Fallot, oxygen-poor blood bypasses the lungs and goes straight out to the body, giving the skin a bluish tint.

question: Why is the antecubital fossa generally avoided for long-term peripheral IV maintenance?

options.A: Bending the elbow can easily kink and block the catheter.
options.B: Medications cannot reach the heart from upper arm veins.
options.C: Infusions run much slower through arm veins than hand veins.
options.D: The veins in this area have no nerve supply nearby.

explanation: Movement at the elbow joint puts constant stress on an IV catheter in the antecubital space, leading to infiltration or flow stoppage. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h2)

question: Which clinical feature is most characteristic of placenta praevia?

options.A: Painless bright red vaginal bleeding
options.B: Rigid, board-like abdomen with no bleeding
options.C: Painful dark red vaginal bleeding
options.D: Continuous clear fluid leakage with cramps

explanation: Placenta praevia typically presents with sudden, painless bleeding consisting of bright red blood because the source is close to the vagina. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h3)

question: What is a very common emotional or social challenge for patients with chronic stress incontinence?

options.A: False belief that they are pregnant
options.B: Uncontrolled aggressive behavior toward caregivers
options.C: Severe memory loss and cognitive decline
options.D: Social isolation and anxiety about public leaks

explanation: The fear of leaking in public can make patients feel embarrassed, causing them to stay home and miss out on social life.

question: What is the main reason for taking a swab (culture and sensitivity) from an infected ear or throat?

options.A: To find the exact germ and the right antibiotic to kill it
options.B: To check for family history of chronic illnesses
options.C: To check the white blood cell count
options.D: To bring down swelling and open up airways

explanation: Culture and sensitivity tests grow the germ in a lab to see which specific drugs will knock out the infection safely.

question: What is the best way to determine if a patient is ready to discuss serious health information?

options.A: Ask for their permission and check what they already know
options.B: Wait until the family demands an update from the doctor
options.C: Assume they want all details because they are in the hospital
options.D: Read the entire medical history before speaking to them

explanation: Asking permission and checking current understanding respects the patient's personal pacing and avoids overwhelming them. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of a living will?

options.A: To grant full medical licensing authority to a trusted family member
options.B: To distribute financial property and land ownership after death
options.C: To name a lawyer who will handle hospital bills and insurance claims
options.D: To outline specific medical treatments a person wants or refuses if terminally ill

explanation: A living will acts as the patient's voice on paper, stating their healthcare choices before they are too sick to speak.

question: What is a primary sign of compassion fatigue in a healthcare worker?

options.A: A sudden increase in physical body weight and strength
options.B: Excessive excitement and eagerness for every shift
options.C: Extraordinary patience with difficult administrative tasks
options.D: Emotional numbness and exhaustion from constant caregiving

explanation: Compassion fatigue happens when exposure to continuous suffering drains a nurse's emotional reserves, causing burnout and detachment. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h7)

question: What makes the intramuscular route absorb medications faster than the subcutaneous route?

options.A: Muscles have a richer blood supply than fat tissue
options.B: Subcutaneous fat repels liquid medications
options.C: Muscle tissue contains more nerve endings
options.D: Injections go straight into the main arteries

explanation: Skeletal muscle has a dense network of blood vessels that quickly take up and distribute injected medications compared to fatty layers. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why must a nurse avoid shaking clean or dirty bed sheets in a hospital ward?

options.A: It causes the cotton fibers to tear and stretch
options.B: It creates static electricity that damages monitors
options.C: It violates facility laundry sorting protocols
options.D: It spreads dust and germs into the surrounding air

explanation: You got it! Shaking sheets sends dust, skin flakes, and bacteria flying into the air, where they can settle on other patients or clean surfaces. Always fold or roll them gently instead!

question: Why should patients always be involved in setting their own rehabilitation goals?

options.A: It ensures the recovery targets matter to the patient's actual daily life.
options.B: It completely removes the need for physical therapy oversight.
options.C: Hospital accreditation rules legally prohibit nurse-only care plans.
options.D: Patients have medical degrees that guide clinical interventions.

explanation: Exactly! When patients help choose what they want to achieve, they feel more motivated to push through tough therapy sessions.

question: Why must a nurse know the exact landmarks of the vulva?

options.A: To pass a urinary catheter without missing the urethra
options.B: To prevent ovarian cysts
options.C: To measure blood pressure correctly
options.D: To track the exact day of ovulation

explanation: Spot on! Knowing your anatomy keeps procedures safe and stops you from accidentally placing a catheter into the vaginal opening instead of the urethra.

question: How do sperm mostly travel upward through the female reproductive tract?

options.A: Riding passively inside the bloodstream after vaginal absorption
options.B: Using their own flagellar motility and uterine muscle contractions
options.C: Crawling along the inner walls using specialized cilia
options.D: Being pushed entirely by gravity when the patient stands

explanation: While sperm use their tails (flagella) to swim, the smooth muscles of the uterus also squeeze rhythmically to help push them along on their journey.

question: What is the main goal when caring for a patient with a secondary metastatic tumour in the heart?

options.A: Palliative care and managing symptoms while treating the primary cancer source
options.B: Preventing the patient from ever moving their arms or legs
options.C: Permanent replacement of all four heart valves with artificial ones
options.D: Complete surgical cure of the heart muscle using a heart transplant

explanation: When cancer has spread from elsewhere, the focus shifts to keeping the patient comfortable, managing symptoms, and treating the original cancer source. Compassionate nursing at its best!

question: Why must men with an enlarged prostate be very careful with central anticholinergics?

options.A: Prostate tissue destroys the active drug instantly
options.B: The medication causes the prostate to shrink too fast
options.C: The drugs can cause or worsen trouble passing urine
options.D: Enlarged prostates absorb the drug too quickly into the blood

explanation: Spot on! By blocking acetylcholine, these drugs relax the bladder muscle and tighten the urinary outlet, making it really hard to pee if the prostate is already blocking things.

question: What is the term when a brain injury causes a client to completely ignore one entire side of their body or room?

options.A: Apraxia
options.B: Unilateral neglect
options.C: Global amnesia
options.D: Expressive aphasia

explanation: Unilateral neglect can feel baffling to the client—their brain literally forgets that one side of the world (or their own body) exists. As nurses, we help bridge that gap!

question: How should you position your patient right after a thoracentesis is finished?

options.A: On the unaffected side
options.B: Prone on the abdomen
options.C: Flat on the back
options.D: Flat on the affected side

explanation: You nailed it! Having them lie on the good (unaffected) side helps the tiny puncture site seal up and lets the treated lung expand fully.

question: A first-time mom has a long second stage of labor with a large baby. What is she most at risk for down there?

options.A: Severe muscle stretching and potential nerve injury
options.B: Immediate permanent tightening of the levator ani
options.C: Hypertrophy and increased muscle strength
options.D: Complete ossification of the pelvic ligaments

explanation: Exactly. Extended pushing and a big baby can really overwork and overstretch the pelvic floor muscles and nerves.

question: While listening to a pregnant patient with a Doppler, you hear a rhythmic sound matching her pulse. What should you do?

options.A: Record this rate immediately as the baby's heart rate
options.B: Assume the fetus has severe bradycardia and prep for emergency
options.C: Recognize this is the maternal pulse and keep searching for the faster fetal heartbeat
options.D: Stop the assessment because the machine is broken

explanation: Great job! Maternal blood vessels run through the uterus, so you always want to double-check that you're counting the baby's heart rate, not mum's.

question: Why do we usually avoid combined estrogen-progestin contraceptives right after childbirth?

options.A: They prevent the uterus from completing normal involution
options.B: They can decrease milk supply and increase blood clot risk
options.C: They cause permanent infertility in nursing mothers
options.D: They stop lochia discharge instantly

explanation: Estrogen can dry up breastmilk production and add to the already high risk of dangerous blood clots that new mothers face. Smart nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h8)

question: What kind of infectious agent causes Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD)?

options.A: A slow-acting bacterial spore
options.B: An abnormally folded prion protein
options.C: A parasitic protozoan in brain tissue
options.D: A mutant strand of DNA virus

explanation: Spot on! CJD is caused by prions, which are unique proteins that misfold and don't even carry DNA or RNA. You've got this!

question: What is another common medical name for synovial fluid aspiration?

options.A: Arthrocentesis
options.B: Paracentesis
options.C: Thoracentesis
options.D: Lumbar puncture

explanation: Arthrocentesis specifically refers to puncturing a joint space to remove fluid for testing or pain relief. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which gland releases gonadotropin-releasing hormone to trigger the female reproductive cycle?

options.A: The anterior pituitary gland
options.B: The adrenal cortex
options.C: The hypothalamus
options.D: The posterior pituitary gland

explanation: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone is synthesized and released by the hypothalamus in the brain to kick off the hormonal cascade. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h1)

question: Why is having a clear 'case definition' so important during a disease outbreak?

options.A: It guarantees that the disease will not spread to neighboring towns.
options.B: It automatically cures the patients who fit the diagnostic description.
options.C: It prevents the government from spending money on laboratory testing.
options.D: It ensures all investigators identify and count cases using the exact same criteria.

explanation: Spot on! A clear case definition makes sure every nurse and doctor is looking for the exact same signs, preventing confusion in our records.

question: What is the main sign of ICT (Information and Communication Technology) addiction?

options.A: A temporary fascination with video games during school holidays
options.B: The physical inability to learn how to operate a personal computer
options.C: An allergic reaction to electromagnetic radiation from screens
options.D: Compulsive use of digital devices that interferes with daily life

explanation: You've got this! ICT addiction happens when device use gets out of hand, starting to affect your schoolwork, daily tasks, and relationships.

question: Why must the nurse immediately label the specimen tubes at the patient's bedside?

options.A: To keep the synovial fluid warm in the room
options.B: To satisfy hospital room cleaning rules
options.C: To help the local anesthetic work faster
options.D: To prevent mixing up samples with another patient

explanation: Immediate labeling at the bedside ensures patient safety and guarantees that laboratory results match the correct client. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why is it so important for nurses to routinely check cranial nerves linked to the special senses?

options.A: Changes in sensory function can indicate early brain injury or increased pressure
options.B: It replaces the need for measuring blood pressure and pulse
options.C: It proves whether the patient is following a healthy daily diet
options.D: It prevents the patient from developing normal age-related hearing loss

explanation: Because cranial nerves plug right into the brain, a sudden change in someone's vision, hearing, or pupil reaction can be an early warning sign that pressure inside the skull is rising.

question: Why should a nurse check the target skin area before applying a prescribed cream?

options.A: To check for signs of breakdown or unexpected infection
options.B: To measure the exact surface area in square centimeters
options.C: To test the electrical conductivity of the skin cells
options.D: To determine if the patient has a systemic fever

explanation: A quick look helps you catch any new irritation or worsening infection before adding more medicine. Patient safety first!

question: What is the main reason for having a patient keep a bladder diary?

options.A: To record fluid intake, leakage episodes, and voiding patterns
options.B: To list all daily medications and food allergies
options.C: To track blood pressure changes throughout the day
options.D: To measure daily weight fluctuations and calorie consumption

explanation: A bladder diary gives you a clear, real-life picture of when the patient drinks, when they leak, and how often they go. Super helpful for planning care!

question: Which of these is NOT a typical safety hazard inside an operating room?

options.A: Sharps injuries from needles and scalpel blades
options.B: Electrical risks from high-powered surgical equipment
options.C: Chemical exposure from waste anesthetic gases
options.D: High-speed public traffic noise from outside the hospital

explanation: You got it! Operating rooms are quiet and sound-proofed. The real worries inside are things like sharps, chemicals, and electrical hazards.

question: Why are daily weight checks such an important nursing tool when managing fluid and electrolyte imbalances?

options.A: Body weight dictates the exact dosage of every routine antibiotic
options.B: Changes in weight provide a reliable daily measure of fluid gain or loss
options.C: Sudden weight loss always proves that kidney function has fully recovered
options.D: Weight records replace the need to monitor urinary output in bedridden patients

explanation: Spot on! A sudden change in weight over 24 hours isn't fat or muscle—it's almost always a shift in body water. Daily weights help us catch fluid overload early!

question: Why are PMTCT programs heavily prioritized in regions like sub-Saharan Africa?

options.A: Pregnant women in this region refuse standard hospital treatment.
options.B: This region bears the highest burden of pediatric HIV infections.
options.C: Antiretroviral drugs are only manufactured on the African continent.
options.D: Other regions have completely eradicated the human immunodeficiency virus.

explanation: Sub-Saharan Africa has the highest prevalence of women living with HIV, making targeted prevention programs crucial in this part of the world. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h1)

question: What do physical therapists mainly focus on during rehabilitation?

options.A: Fine motor coordination and cooking skills
options.B: Emotional coping and mental health support
options.C: Large muscle movements and lower body walking
options.D: Speech articulation and swallowing safety

explanation: Think of PTs as the experts on big movements! They focus on large muscles, balance, walking, and helping patients move around safely.

question: Which of the following should a nurse NOT do in end-of-life care?

options.A: Respecting the cultural and spiritual wishes of the family
options.B: Supporting the family through the grieving process
options.C: Withholding pain medication out of fear of addiction in a dying patient
options.D: Providing comfort measures and meticulous hygiene

explanation: Never hold back pain relief! At the end of life, our main duty is comfort. Addiction is not a worry when managing pain for a dying patient.

question: As a nurse, why should you look at growth trends over time rather than just a single weight check?

options.A: A single measurement cannot show whether a teen is following their expected growth curve.
options.B: Single measurements are legally invalid for minors in healthcare settings.
options.C: Scales in clinics are rarely calibrated for adolescent body weights.
options.D: Weight changes too slowly to be measured during a routine annual checkup.

explanation: Spot on! Checking weight across multiple visits helps you spot sudden jumps or drops that might signal a health or nutrition issue.

question: How much extra stockinette length should generally be cut beyond the planned cast area?

options.A: At least 5 meters for safety
options.B: 10 to 15 centimeters at each end
options.C: Exactly 2 millimeters total
options.D: No extra length at all

explanation: Leaving 10 to 15 centimeters of extra stockinette at both ends is necessary so the edges can be folded back over the cast later. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary danger of running out of injection safety commodities at a health clinic?

options.A: Clinicians may resort to reusing single-use equipment.
options.B: Medications will automatically expire much faster.
options.C: The cost of electricity at the facility will increase.
options.D: Patients will completely stop visiting the facility for care.

explanation: When basic injection supplies run out, desperate staff may unfortunately reuse disposable syringes, spreading infections. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h1)

question: Why is the antenatal clinic card given to the pregnant woman to carry around herself?

options.A: Because clinics are not allowed to store paper records on site
options.B: To prove she has paid all her hospital bills in advance
options.C: To serve as a ticket for free meals at the hospital canteen
options.D: So any healthcare worker can review her history during an emergency

explanation: If an emergency happens away from her regular clinic, any nurse or doctor can instantly check her medical history right off her personal card!

question: Why is rational drug use so important in the fight against antibiotic resistance?

options.A: It ensures that pharmaceutical companies make higher profits annually
options.B: It guarantees that all drugs are manufactured using local herbs only
options.C: It stops patients from ever visiting a public health facility again
options.D: It prevents the overuse and misuse of antibiotics that cause bacteria to mutate

explanation: Spot on! Using antibiotics wisely stops germs from learning how to beat our drugs.

question: What does 'cohorting' mean in the ward?

options.A: Placing patients with the same infection in the same room
options.B: Training new nursing students in isolation procedures
options.C: Sharing medical equipment between different hospital wards
options.D: Moving a patient to a room with negative air pressure

explanation: When single rooms run out, grouping patients with the exact same infection together is a smart way to manage space and safety.

question: A young woman with a history of FGM comes to the clinic with lower tummy pain and painful urination. What is a likely cause?

options.A: Excessive estrogen production
options.B: Chronic urinary tract infections from scarring
options.C: Early-onset menopause
options.D: Congenital kidney failure

explanation: You nailed it! Scarring and altered anatomy from FGM can block normal urine flow, making infections and pain much more likely.

question: What is the primary reason for recommending a low-sodium diet in cardiac prevention?

options.A: It prevents the liver from producing too much cholesterol
options.B: It reduces fluid retention and lowers blood pressure
options.C: It stops the pancreas from releasing excess insulin
options.D: It increases the amount of dietary fiber in the gut

explanation: Excess sodium holds extra fluid in the blood vessels, increasing the pressure against arterial walls and forcing the heart to work harder. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h3)

question: Where do we usually place a peripheral arterial line?

options.A: Carotid artery
options.B: Radial artery
options.C: Femoral vein
options.D: Brachial vein

explanation: The radial artery at the wrist is our go-to spot because it is easy to reach and has great backup blood supply (collateral circulation).

question: Why does supine hypotension happen when a pregnant woman lies flat on her back?

options.A: Heart rate drops dangerously low to rest the cardiac muscle
options.B: The lungs expand too much and trap excess oxygen away from the tissues
options.C: The heavy uterus presses on the major blood vessels returning blood to the heart
options.D: Progesterone instantly widens all peripheral blood vessels in the upper body

explanation: The weight of the pregnant uterus compresses the inferior vena cava, blocking blood flow back to the heart and causing blood pressure to drop. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h1)

question: At what point should waste sorting (segregation) happen in the clinical ward?

options.A: At the end of the nursing shift
options.B: When the cleaner arrives with large trucks
options.C: After the waste reaches the municipal dump
options.D: Immediately at the point of generation

explanation: Spot on! Sorting waste right where you use it prevents dangerous mix-ups and keeps everyone handling it safe.

question: What is the biggest danger that causes high complications in unsafe abortions?

options.A: Early detection of pregnancy in a regulated hospital setting
options.B: The use of untrained providers and unsterile conditions
options.C: Regular monitoring by professional obstetric nurses
options.D: The prescription of standard medical abortion pills by doctors

explanation: Unsafe abortions often involve dirty tools and untrained people, which sadly leads to heavy infections and severe bleeding.

question: Which of these is a classic feature of a benign tumor?

options.A: It grows very fast and invades nearby muscle
options.B: It has poorly differentiated, weird-looking cells
options.C: It easily spreads through the lymphatic system
options.D: It stays localized inside a fibrous capsule

explanation: Benign is friendly! These tumors stay neatly wrapped up in their own little capsule and don't try to invade the surrounding tissues.

question: Why is washing a mammalian bite wound with high-pressure water so important?

options.A: Water pressure chemically breaks down residual animal saliva in the tissue
options.B: Animal mouths harbor diverse bacteria that easily cause deep tissue infections
options.C: It permanently seals open blood vessels to stop bleeding immediately
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any tetanus prophylaxis

explanation: Animal and human mouths carry lots of germs. Flushing deep bite wounds thoroughly helps wash away bacteria before they cause ugly infections.

question: What is the main difference between civil liability and criminal liability for a nurse?

options.A: Criminal liability is resolved through financial compensation to the patient.
options.B: Criminal liability addresses offenses against the state punishable by jail or fines.
options.C: Civil liability only applies to doctors, never to registered nurses.
options.D: Civil liability involves state imprisonment while criminal involves apologies.

explanation: Criminal law deals with public safety offences prosecuted by the state (like jail time or fines), whereas civil law is usually about private disputes and compensation. Good to know for practice!

question: Which gastrostomy feeding method uses an electronic pump to deliver formula slowly over 24 hours?

options.A: Continuous feeding
options.B: Gravity drip feeding
options.C: Bolus feeding
options.D: Intermittent feeding

explanation: Continuous feeding runs at a slow, steady hourly rate throughout the day and night using a mechanical pump. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h4)

question: On her third day after delivery, a patient complains that her right calf is painful, swollen, and feels warmer than the left. What is the most important thing you should do?

options.A: Encourage her to walk briskly around the hospital corridor
options.B: Massage the calf firmly to break up any muscle cramps
options.C: Apply an ice pack directly to the painful calf muscle
options.D: Instruct the patient to stay off her feet and notify the physician immediately

explanation: This sounds like a deep vein thrombosis (blood clot). Never massage a suspected clot, as it could break loose and travel to the lungs—always keep the patient resting and call the doctor right away!

question: Why is the smoke that comes off tissues during laser or electrocautery surgery considered a health hazard?

options.A: It immediately trips the circuit breaker in theatre monitors
options.B: It instantly blinds anyone not wearing dark glasses
options.C: It can carry tiny live virus particles, tissue bits, and toxic gases
options.D: It stains the surgical gowns and patient skin permanently

explanation: When tissues are burned away by heat, they release a smoke plume into the air that carries microscopic debris and chemicals you definitely don't want to breathe in.

question: Which of these is NOT a common cause of oesophagitis (inflammation of the food pipe)?

options.A: Excessive production of thyroid hormones
options.B: Fungal or viral infections in weakened immune systems
options.C: Prolonged contact with harsh stomach acid
options.D: Certain harsh oral tablets taken with no water

explanation: Spot on! Thyroid issues affect your metabolism, but they don't directly burn or irritate the lining of your oesophagus the way acid, pills, or infections do.

question: What is the primary danger of leaving a prepared, diluted injection unlabeled on a medication cart?

options.A: The medicine will automatically change into a solid block
options.B: The plastic barrel of the syringe will dissolve within minutes
options.C: Another healthcare worker might administer the wrong drug or dose
options.D: The expiration date of the diluent will immediately reset

explanation: Unlabeled medications invite administration errors, as staff cannot verify what substance, concentration, or patient the syringe belongs to. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h6)

question: As a nurse, what is our main goal when trying to stop a secondary injury after head trauma?

options.A: To permanently numb the patient to eliminate all pain
options.B: To reverse the torn nerve fibers caused by the initial crash
options.C: To prevent further cell death by maintaining oxygen and blood flow
options.D: To repair fractured skull bones without surgery

explanation: Well done! Since we can't always undo the initial impact, our nursing care focuses heavily on keeping oxygen and blood flowing so swelling doesn't destroy more brain cells.

question: A recovering heart patient is ready to take their first walk down the ward corridor. What should you do?

options.A: Attach a portable telemetry or wireless monitoring unit
options.B: Keep the patient attached to a heavy wall-mounted monitor with long cables
options.C: Wait until the patient returns to the bed to check vitals
options.D: Disconnect all monitoring devices to encourage normal movement

explanation: Early walks are great for recovery, but we always want a wireless or telemetry unit attached so we can safely watch out for any exercise-related heart issues.

question: What is one of the earliest psychological signs that a patient is entering shock?

options.A: Extreme euphoria
options.B: Deep, heavy snoring
options.C: Sudden memory loss
options.D: Restlessness and anxiety

explanation: As oxygen delivery to the brain decreases, patients often become restless, anxious, or confused before losing consciousness. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is the medical term for when the kidneys stop producing urine altogether at the end of life?

options.A: Polyuria
options.B: Anuria
options.C: Dysuria
options.D: Hematuria

explanation: Anuria means complete lack of urine production because blood flow to the kidneys has slowed to a stop. You're mastering your medical terms!

question: Why do misplaced endometrial implants cause ongoing pain and scarring in the pelvis?

options.A: They grow rapidly into malignant tumors within weeks
options.B: They release massive amounts of male hormones into the abdomen
options.C: They bleed during each cycle, causing local inflammation and adhesions
options.D: They destroy the nerves supplying the lower abdominal wall

explanation: Wherever these misplaced cells land, they still respond to monthly hormones by trying to 'bleed'. This trapped blood irritates nearby tissue, causing painful inflammation and sticky scar tissue.

question: Why is keeping the call bell right next to the patient so important for safe bathroom care?

options.A: It controls the room lighting and temperature automatically
options.B: It allows the patient to call for help before attempting risky, unassisted bathroom trips
options.C: It stops the patient from ever needing a bedpan during the night shift
options.D: It ensures the nurse can check the patient's telephone messages quickly

explanation: A reachable call bell is a fall-prevention tool! It reminds patients they don't have to struggle alone and encourages them to call you instead of risking a dangerous fall.

question: On a standard muscle strength scale, what does a score of zero (0) indicate?

options.A: A slight flicker of movement only
options.B: No movement or muscle contraction at all
options.C: Movement is possible against gravity
options.D: Normal strength against full resistance

explanation: A score of zero means there is total paralysis or no visible muscle movement when the patient tries to move.

question: Why does the nervous system use electrical impulses for communication?

options.A: To store long-term memories in the blood
options.B: To provide rapid and specific responses to body changes
options.C: To produce hormones for the digestive tract
options.D: To filter waste products out of the brain

explanation: Electrical impulses allow the body to react almost immediately to internal and external stimuli, which is essential for survival. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why is skin turgor checked over the clavicle or forearm during a physical assessment?

options.A: To evaluate the patient's overall hydration status
options.B: To measure the exact blood pressure in the upper body
options.C: To check for localized muscle weakness under the skin
options.D: To determine if the patient has a superficial fungal infection

explanation: Skin turgor reflects how quickly the skin returns to its normal flat position, which helps nurses estimate body fluid volume and hydration. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h1)

question: A patient has chronic open-angle glaucoma. Which part of their vision usually fades first?

options.A: Upper vertical vision only
options.B: Side (peripheral) vision
options.C: Central vision
options.D: Color vision

explanation: Correct! Open-angle glaucoma is sneaky; it slowly steals side vision first, long before the person notices any trouble with their central view.

question: Why must nurses wear gloves or use a tool when applying certain topical medications?

options.A: To keep the patient's room completely sterile
options.B: To prevent absorbing the medication through their own skin
options.C: To prevent the patient from feeling cold during touch
options.D: To ensure the medication absorbs faster into the patient

explanation: Powerful drugs like hormone creams can soak right through your bare hands if you aren't wearing gloves. Always protect yourself too!

question: Why is it important to note if a patient frequently strains during bowel movements?

options.A: Constipation directly damages the pudendal nerve roots in the lower spine
options.B: Bowel movements have no connection to pelvic floor health
options.C: Chronic straining places continuous downward pressure and stretches pelvic muscles
options.D: Straining causes the kidneys to produce excess urine

explanation: You nailed it! Pushing too hard over time stretches out those supportive muscles and fascia, weakening the whole sling.

question: Why must anticholinergic anti-spasmodics be strictly avoided in patients with narrow-angle glaucoma?

options.A: They paralyze the muscles that move the eyeball
options.B: They dry out the tear ducts completely
options.C: They cause permanent blindness within one hour
options.D: They can dangerously increase eye pressure

explanation: Anticholinergics affect how the eye drains fluid. In glaucoma patients, this can trigger a dangerous spike in pressure inside the eye.

question: A nurse notices an unsteady resident pacing near a cluttered hallway. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Administer a strong sedative medication to keep the resident asleep
options.B: Ignore the situation since walking independently is always encouraged
options.C: Clear the hallway clutter and assist the resident safely back to their seat
options.D: Instruct the resident to run down the hallway to improve agility

explanation: You've got it! Clearing out obstacles right away is a quick, life-saving step to prevent falls.

question: A nurse hears crackling sounds in a patient's lungs, and the patient feels breathless. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: A simple chest cold with thick mucus
options.B: An allergic reaction to hospital blankets
options.C: Normal breathing sounds for a resting adult
options.D: Fluid backing up into the lungs due to failing heart function

explanation: Those crackles are the sound of tiny air sacs popping open through a layer of fluid. Because the left side of the heart isn't pumping blood forward, fluid leaks right into the lungs.

question: What does antimicrobial resistance actually mean?

options.A: Immune systems destroying white blood cells
options.B: The human body rejecting prescribed vitamins
options.C: Microorganisms evolving to survive standard medications
options.D: Bacteria growing faster in cold temperatures

explanation: You've got this! Resistance simply means germs change and adapt so that drugs like antibiotics can no longer destroy them.

question: As a student nurse doing chest compressions, how do you make sure blood keeps filling the heart between pushes?

options.A: Leaning slightly on the chest to save energy
options.B: Compressing the sternum as deeply as possible
options.C: Allowing full chest recoil after every compression
options.D: Slowing down the compression rate to 60 per minute

explanation: Make sure to lift your weight completely off the chest after each push. This lets blood flow back into the heart chambers ready for the next squeeze!

question: Why are antibiotics often NOT needed after successfully draining a simple, small skin abscess?

options.A: The body destroys the remaining bacteria within minutes
options.B: Antibiotics cannot travel through the blood to skin tissues
options.C: Skin bacteria are naturally immune to all oral medications
options.D: Physical removal of the pus cures the localized infection

explanation: Once you drain the trapped pus out of a simple abscess, the body's natural immune system is usually strong enough to take care of the rest all on its own!

question: Which principle ensures that vulnerable and quiet voices are heard during community health projects?

options.A: Equity
options.B: Profit
options.C: Isolation
options.D: Speed

explanation: Equity makes sure that everyone, especially the poor and marginalized, gets a fair chance to participate and benefit. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h2)

question: Which action best shows you are advocating for your patient at the end of life?

options.A: Withholding pain medication to keep the patient awake for visiting relatives
options.B: Ignoring advance directives if the attending physician disagrees with them
options.C: Ensuring a documented DNR order is followed despite objections from distant relatives
options.D: Following the loudest family member's demand to start aggressive CPR

explanation: As a nurse, your duty is to protect the patient's documented wishes, even when family members disagree.

question: Why is spotting a high-risk labour early on so important for us as nurses?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any postpartum medication
options.B: It allows the hospital to discharge the patient within one hour
options.C: It guarantees the mother will experience a painless delivery
options.D: It prevents small problems from turning into life-threatening emergencies

explanation: Spotting risks early is a superpower in nursing! It gives our team time to step in before a small issue turns into a major crisis.

question: What is the biggest advantage of having a separate casualty theatre in the hospital?

options.A: It completely removes the need for sterilization protocols
options.B: It reduces the number of doctors required on duty
options.C: It allows student nurses to perform surgeries independently
options.D: It preserves major operating theatres for complex and major surgeries

explanation: You nailed it! Separating minor cases from major ones ensures our heavy-duty ORs are always ready when a major surgical emergency rolls in.

question: Which of these is a well-known chemical hazard you might find in a clinical area?

options.A: Discarded paper patient admission folders
options.B: Cardboard packaging from intravenous fluids
options.C: Used cotton wool rolls from wound dressing
options.D: Mercury from a broken blood pressure device

explanation: Correct! Heavy metals like mercury—often found in older BP cuffs or thermometers—are toxic chemicals that need careful cleanup if spilled.

question: Why is it important for a nurse to ask about oral and anal sexual practices during a check-up?

options.A: Clients expect nurses to document their personal lifestyle choices for insurance
options.B: Urethral swabs are sensitive enough to detect infections in all other body parts
options.C: Infections can transmit across different mucosal sites and require site-specific testing
options.D: Standard blood tests will automatically cover all anatomical exposure sites

explanation: Germs don't just stay in the genitals! If a patient had oral or anal exposure, we need swabs from the throat or rectum to catch the infection accurately.

question: What usually causes Transfusion-Associated Circulatory Overload (TACO)?

options.A: A mismatched ABO blood type between donor and recipient
options.B: Bacterial contamination of the red blood cells during storage
options.C: An allergic response to donor plasma proteins in the blood bag
options.D: Infusing blood too rapidly for the patient's cardiovascular system to handle

explanation: TACO happens when fluid goes in faster than a patient's heart can pump it, causing fluid backup in the lungs.

question: What is your very first nursing action if a patient starts bleeding heavily right after birth?

options.A: Massage the uterus and call for emergency assistance
options.B: Wait for laboratory results before taking any action
options.C: Send the patient home to rest in bed
options.D: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward

explanation: Act fast! Massaging the uterus makes it clamp down and stop the bleeding, while shouting for help brings your team running.

question: A patient with a family history of brain degeneration starts accusing relatives of stealing items they just misplaced. What is this called?

options.A: Psychosis
options.B: Depression
options.C: Anxiety
options.D: Apathy

explanation: Exactly. Developing false beliefs or paranoia means the person is losing touch with reality, which is a classic psychotic symptom of the disease. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h3)

question: What is the medical word for when a patient is taking many different medications at the same time?

options.A: Potentiation
options.B: Bioavailability
options.C: Polypharmacy
options.D: Pharmacodynamics

explanation: "Poly" means many, and "pharmacy" refers to drugs. Polypharmacy simply means a patient is juggling multiple medications, which raises the chance of drug clashes.

question: Why do we encourage new mothers to get up and walk around (ambulate) early after childbirth?

options.A: To speed up the immediate closure of the cervix
options.B: To reduce the risk of blood clots and improve circulation
options.C: To encourage the baby to sleep through the night
options.D: To prevent the mother from producing too much colostrum

explanation: Getting moving gets the blood pumping! It keeps circulation strong and stops blood from pooling in the legs, preventing dangerous clots. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h7)

question: Which part of the digestive tract does ulcerative colitis mainly affect?

options.A: The entire small intestine
options.B: The colon and rectum
options.C: The mouth and esophagus
options.D: The stomach and duodenum

explanation: Ulcerative colitis stays in the large intestine. It starts down in the rectum and can spread upward in a steady, continuous line.

question: Why is getting the partner's approval emphasized so heavily during family planning counseling?

options.A: Ignoring it can lead to domestic conflict and discontinuation
options.B: The law requires men to test the medicine first
options.C: Husbands must sign a legal contract for every pill
options.D: Women are not allowed to touch medical items

question: Which imaging test uses a strong magnetic field instead of X-rays to picture soft tissues?

options.A: Magnetic resonance imaging

options.C: Plain skull X-ray
options.D: Computed tomography scan

question: What exactly is Sheehan's syndrome?

options.A: Immune system attack on the adrenal glands brought on by stress
options.B: Death of pituitary tissue due to severe blood loss right after childbirth
options.C: A benign tumor causing sudden vision loss in older men

question: If a field worker is doing a household survey to find out about maternal deaths without using confusing medical terms, how should they ask?

options.C: Did any woman in this house die while pregnant, during delivery, or shortly after childbirth?
options.D: Did any woman experience a complete termination of reproductive biomarkers last year?

explanation: Using clear, everyday language about pregnancy timing helps families easily understand and share accurate information without needing a medical degree!

question: What is the correct sequence for a physical respiratory examination?

options.A: Palpation, auscultation, inspection, percussion

options.C: Inspection, palpation, percussion, auscultation

question: You are helping a patient with severe bradykinesia get ready in the morning. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Withholding morning medication until physical therapy is finished

options.C: Completing all hygiene tasks quickly for the patient to save time
options.D: Restricting oral fluid intake to prevent frequent bathroom trips

question: A patient has a severe spinal cord injury needing advanced surgery. Where should they be sent?

options.A: Outpatient clinic
options.B: Community post
options.C: Tertiary level
options.D: Primary level

question: What is the main clue that tells you a patient has Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) rather than regular stress?

options.A: The patient experiences complete memory loss during stressful events.
options.B: The symptoms only appear when the person is exposed to bright lights.
options.C: The physical symptoms include high fever and joint stiffness.

question: What is another common medical name for hydatid disease?

question: When is using an indwelling catheter most necessary?

options.A: To treat a mild, uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection
options.B: For managing stress incontinence during daytime activities
options.C: As a convenient alternative for an elderly patient who dislikes walking
options.D: For accurate urine output monitoring in a critically ill patient

question: Why do growing pituitary tumors often cause vision changes like trouble seeing out of the sides of your eyes?

options.C: High pressure inside the skull damages the back part of the brain directly.

question: Why is writing accurate and prompt notes so crucial in an intensive care setting?

options.A: It allows family members to edit the medical chart from home
options.B: It provides a clear record of rapid changes and treatment responses for the whole team
options.C: It guarantees that the hospital insurance claim will never be denied
options.D: It replaces the need for verbal handoffs during shift changes entirely

explanation: ICU patients change fast! Good documentation ensures that the next nurse or doctor stepping into the unit knows exactly what happened and how the patient responded.

question: Which scope procedure lets the doctor look directly inside the uterine cavity?

options.A: Colposcopy

question: What can happen if the pelvic ligaments and fascia become weak?

options.A: Blood flow to the lower limbs is cut off

question: What is the main aim of disaster preparedness in a community?

options.A: To prevent natural weather events from ever occurring
options.B: To relocate all community residents to permanent urban centers
options.C: To ensure hospitals make a profit during unexpected crises
options.D: To minimize injury, loss of life, and disruption during an emergency

explanation: While we can't stop storms or floods, good planning helps keep people safe and cuts down the damage when disaster hits.

question: Why does a woman usually reach a higher blood alcohol concentration than a man after drinking the exact same amount?

question: A patient who previously had a secretive abortion now struggles with recurrent miscarriages in her second trimester. What underlying issue should you suspect?

options.B: Chronic renal failure from past chemical toxicity

question: Roughly how long does the complete cycle of spermatogenesis take in humans?

question: How does the VAPP Act change how society and the law view domestic abuse within homes?

question: Why does pregnancy put a woman with sickle cell disease at higher risk for complications?

question: Why might a patient with a severe vitamin B12 deficiency feel numbness or tingling in their hands and feet?

options.B: The patient is experiencing a sudden adverse reaction to food
options.C: Red blood cells press directly against the spinal cord
options.D: Low vitamins cause the blood vessels in the fingers to instantly shrink

question: What is the biggest risk you watch out for at skeletal traction pin sites?

options.C: Complete numbness of the entire unaffected leg

question: Why is a baseline neurological assessment important for a patient admitted with a head injury?

options.B: To replace the need for physician examinations
options.C: To eliminate the need for ongoing vital sign monitoring
options.D: To diagnose the exact microscopic cellular damage present

question: Which tiny blood vessels are responsible for directly trading gases and nutrients with your body tissues?

options.A: Aorta

options.D: Capillaries

explanation: Capillaries are like the microscopic trading posts of your circulatory system. Their walls are super thin so oxygen and nutrients can easily slip across to your cells.

question: A client on birth control calls complaining of sudden, severe pain and swelling in just one calf. What is your best nursing advice?

question: Why are patients told to drink water and hold their urine before a pelvic ultrasound?

options.B: To encourage bowel movements before the scan

question: A home care nurse is reviewing proper maintenance with a client who uses a metered-dose inhaler. What instruction should the nurse include?

question: Why do heavy workloads and staff fatigue make patient harm more likely?

options.B: They legally exempt hospitals from following standard infection control
options.C: They prevent nurses from documenting vital signs on paper charts

explanation: You nailed it! When nurses or doctors are exhausted and stressed, their mental focus drops, making it easier to miss important clinical signs.

question: Why is sudden, heavy postpartum bleeding that causes dizziness treated as a top emergency?

options.A: It prevents the mother from producing enough breast milk
options.B: It quickly leads to hypovolemic shock and organ failure
options.C: It always results in permanent damage to the kidneys

question: Which of these practices is NOT part of safe umbilical cord care taught by nurses?

options.A: Applying animal dung to stop bleeding

options.D: Keeping the cord stump dry and uncovered

question: When does monitoring of a community health program actually happen?

question: You realize you forgot to document a vital medication given two hours ago. What should you do?

question: What is the main goal of using traction for a fracture?

options.C: To dissolve blood clots that form inside the injured blood vessels

question: Which of these conditions is most likely to need a surgical valve repair or replacement?

options.B: Severe aortic stenosis

options.D: Mild sinus tachycardia

question: What details should you write down in the chart after doing passive range of motion exercises?

options.B: The patient's favorite food and religious beliefs

question: Why can psychological abuse be just as damaging as physical abuse?

question: Which hormone directly builds up and thickens the uterine lining during the first half of the cycle?

options.D: Progesterone

question: Why is it helpful for a nurse to check how much menstrual pain affects a patient's daily routine?

options.A: To determine how severely the pain interferes with the patient's life
options.B: To decide whether the patient needs immediate emergency surgery
options.C: To prove to the physician that the patient is exaggerating symptoms

question: Why does poor nutrition make HIV progress faster?

question: Which of these is considered an extrinsic cause of a restrictive lung disease?

question: Which internal organ is frequently damaged alongside the joints in untreated chronic gout?

question: What type of motivation drives a nurse who feels a deep personal pride and joy in helping patients recover?

question: Why must patients take off all jewelry and metal objects before a CT scan?

options.B: Metal heats up dangerously during the scan process

question: A client with a terminal degenerative disorder can still speak clearly. When should you discuss advance directives and end-of-life wishes with them?

options.C: Only after the client loses consciousness in the final hours of life
options.D: During the initial diagnostic blood test before the disease is explained

explanation: It is best to discuss advance directives early while the client is still of sound mind to ensure their personal wishes are truly honored.

question: Which of the following is an example of a long-acting reversible contraceptive (LARC) method?

options.A: Combined oral contraceptive pills
options.B: Subdermal contraceptive implants
options.C: Male latex barrier condoms
options.D: Spermicidal foaming vaginal tablets

explanation: Exactly! Implants and IUDs offer long-term protection against pregnancy, but can be easily removed whenever the client is ready.

question: Before the treaty, why did companies love to ship toxic waste to other countries?

options.A: Shipping companies received government tax breaks for exports
options.B: Developing nations had weak laws and lower disposal costs
options.C: Poorer countries urgently needed industrial ash for road building
options.D: Developing nations specifically requested toxic chemicals for farming

explanation: Exactly! Safe waste disposal is expensive. Companies saved money by taking advantage of countries that didn't yet have strict environmental laws.

question: What is the main benefit of grouping drugs by their therapeutic use?

options.A: It groups medications that treat similar medical conditions together
options.B: It dictates the exact manufacturing cost of the chemical compound
options.C: It proves which brand name version of the drug is superior
options.D: It eliminates the need for any pharmacokinetic testing in humans

explanation: Exactly! Therapeutic classification helps us easily see which drugs treat which illnesses.

question: During a CT scan with contrast, a patient suddenly develops widespread hives, facial swelling, and mild wheezing. What is your immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Ask the patient to hold their breath until the scanning is finished.
options.B: Stop the contrast injection and notify the medical team immediately.
options.C: Reassure the patient that hives are a completely normal side effect.
options.D: Administer a dose of oral pain medication to calm the patient.

explanation: Hives and wheezing indicate an allergic reaction to the contrast media, requiring the immediate cessation of the infusion and prompt emergency medical intervention. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h4)

question: You are caring for a 38-week pregnant mother with many past deliveries who also has severe anemia. What is the best delivery recommendation?

options.A: Advise delivery at a well-equipped hospital that has blood transfusion services.
options.B: Wait for spontaneous labor at home until contractions are very close.
options.C: Plan a home birth attended by a traditional birth attendant.
options.D: Encourage unassisted labor to avoid medical interventions.

explanation: Because she has a high risk of heavy bleeding and low blood count, she needs to deliver where doctors and nurses can easily give blood or emergency care.

question: When a patient complains of 'pruritus' during a health history, what are they experiencing?

options.A: Nail bed separation
options.B: Unusual skin darkening
options.C: Severe itching
options.D: Hair thinning

explanation: Pruritus is just the medical word for a deep, uncomfortable urge to scratch your skin. You've got this!

question: What is the primary purpose of cerebrospinal fluid within the ventricles?

options.A: To generate electrical action potentials for nerve fibers
options.B: To produce hormones that regulate body temperature
options.C: To cushion the brain and provide mechanical protection
options.D: To supply thick insulating myelin to the spinal cord

explanation: Cerebrospinal fluid acts as a shock absorber, shielding the brain from impact against the skull bones. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is one of the best long-term ways to improve maternal health in developing countries?

options.A: Relying entirely on traditional birth attendants
options.B: Improving female education and socio-economic empowerment
options.C: Banning family planning services
options.D: Closing all primary health clinics in rural zones

explanation: Educating and empowering women changes everything! When women have a voice and education, they make healthier choices and access care much earlier.

question: Why is it important to have family caregivers demonstrate tube care before hospital discharge?

options.A: To legally transfer full liability for the medical device to the family
options.B: To confirm they can safely perform procedures and handle problems at home
options.C: To prove they do not need any further help from home health nurses
options.D: To test whether they can afford expensive commercial feeding pumps

explanation: Return demonstrations ensure that family members have practical competence and confidence to manage tube feedings safely without professional supervision. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h8)

question: What is the standard first-line medication for treating long-term hypothyroidism?

options.A: Levothyroxine
options.B: Propylthiouracil
options.C: Methimazole
options.D: Propranolol

explanation: Correct! Levothyroxine is a synthetic hormone that safely replaces what the natural thyroid isn't making enough of.

question: A patient's chest tube accidentally slips out of the drainage machine. What is your very first nursing move?

options.A: Call the physician immediately before taking action
options.B: Immerse the end of the chest tube in sterile water
options.C: Remove the dressing and inspect the insertion site
options.D: Clamp the chest tube securely with metal hemostats

explanation: Plunging the tube into sterile water instantly recreates a water seal and stops room air from rushing into the chest. Quick thinking saves lives here!

question: A patient with severe liver disease is prescribed a medication that is normally broken down by hepatic enzymes. What is the most appropriate nursing concern?

options.A: The liver disease will instantly cure itself once the pill is swallowed
options.B: The drug may build up in the body and cause toxic effects
options.C: The medication will pass through the body without any effect at all
options.D: The drug will be eliminated too quickly to provide any relief

explanation: A damaged liver cannot metabolize drugs effectively, leading to dangerous levels accumulating in the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h4)

question: You are about to give a patient a drug with a dosage you aren't sure about. What should you do?

options.A: Check the formulary or drug guide to confirm the correct safe dosage range
options.B: Administer the medication immediately to avoid delaying ward routines
options.C: Throw the medication away in the clinical waste bin without telling anyone
options.D: Ask another patient in the same ward what dose they usually take

explanation: Always double-check! Consulting a trusted drug guide keeps your patient safe and builds your clinical confidence.

question: Which common food item must a patient avoid before doing a stool occult blood test?

options.A: Green tea
options.B: White rice
options.C: Red meat
options.D: Boiled yam

explanation: You nailed it! Red meat has hemoglobin that can mess with the test chemicals and give a false-positive result.

question: Why do nursing students learn about population birth trends?

options.A: To calculate national financial budgets for the government
options.B: To accurately predict community maternal and child healthcare needs
options.C: To determine international trade policies for medical goods
options.D: To replace the work of civil registrars and census officers

explanation: You got it! Knowing birth rates helps you anticipate how many mothers and babies will need care in your facility.

question: Which part of the peripheral nervous system controls voluntary skeletal muscle movement?

options.A: Somatic nervous system
options.B: Parasympathetic division
options.C: Sympathetic division
options.D: Autonomic nervous system

explanation: The somatic system is responsible for conscious control over skeletal muscles. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the main reason for explaining each step of the exam to the patient?

options.A: To fulfill a legal requirement for surgical consent
options.B: To reduce anxiety and build trust between nurse and patient
options.C: To train the patient to perform their own physical assessment
options.D: To speed up the total time spent at the bedside

explanation: Clear communication helps the patient relax, making the assessment easier and more accurate. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h2)

question: Which symptom is a classic indicator that prompts a doctor to order a fasting blood sugar test?

options.A: Sudden low blood pressure and dizziness
options.B: Excessive thirst and frequent urination
options.C: Swelling in the lower legs and ankles
options.D: Yellowing of the skin and eyes

explanation: Polydipsia and polyuria are hallmark signs of high blood sugar that signal the need for diagnostic screening. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h3)

question: What is another common term for a congenital anomaly?

options.A: A degenerative illness
options.B: A birth defect
options.C: An infectious disease
options.D: An acquired injury

explanation: Congenital anomalies are physical or functional abnormalities present from birth, which is why they are commonly called birth defects. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h1)

question: The place where a microorganism normally lives and multiplies is called what?

options.A: A susceptible host
options.B: A reservoir
options.C: A portal of entry
options.D: A transmission route

explanation: A reservoir provides a safe home for pathogens to survive and multiply before finding a new host. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h2)

question: Which emergency medication must a nurse have ready right away if a patient starts having a severe allergic reaction to the dye?

options.A: Insulin regular
options.B: Furosemide
options.C: Morphine sulfate
options.D: Epinephrine

explanation: Epinephrine is the lifesaving go-to drug for severe allergic reactions because it quickly opens up airways and supports blood pressure.

question: Which special cells in the lining of the intestine make protective mucus?

options.A: Parietal cells
options.B: Stem cells
options.C: Chief cells
options.D: Goblet cells

explanation: Goblet cells look like little wine goblets and pump out mucus to keep the gut lining slippery and safe from harsh digestive juices.

question: What does the intraarticular route of medication administration involve?

options.A: Delivering drugs through the skin using a patch
options.B: Swallowing pills for systemic joint relief
options.C: Administering medicine into a muscle belly
options.D: Injecting medication directly into a joint space

question: Which of these charting entries is poorly written?

options.D: Patient appears to be in a very bad mood today

explanation: Correct! Vague labels like 'bad mood' are judgmental. Always write down the exact behaviors you observe instead.

question: Why do drugs with a narrow therapeutic index need very careful blood monitoring?

options.A: The safe dose is very close to the toxic dose.
options.B: They can only be given through intravenous infusion.
options.C: They stop working after three days of administration.
options.D: The patient builds resistance to them very quickly.

explanation: With a narrow therapeutic index, the line between 'helping' and 'harming' is very thin. Careful monitoring keeps our patients safe!

question: What body regulates the Nurse Practice Act and professional standards for nurses in Nigeria?

options.D: Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare

question: Where are the parathyroid glands located?

question: What is the primary focus of preventive nursing in musculoskeletal health?

options.A: Surgical repair of broken bones

options.C: Stopping injuries before they happen
options.D: Treating chronic joint infections

explanation: Preventive nursing aims to identify risks and educate patients to stop musculoskeletal problems before they develop. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h1)

question: Which of these common items can block your body from absorbing oral levothyroxine?

options.A: Antacids containing calcium or aluminum
options.B: Inhaled bronchodilators for asthma
options.C: Broad-spectrum antibiotics like penicillin
options.D: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs

explanation: Minerals like calcium and aluminum act like magnets in your stomach, grabbing onto the levothyroxine and stopping it from entering your blood.

question: Why do doctors frequently prescribe corticosteroid medications to patients with brain tumors?

options.A: To reduce brain swelling and intracranial pressure
options.B: To cure the underlying cancer cells completely
options.C: To lower the patient's blood pressure levels
options.D: To prevent the patient from developing an infection

explanation: Well done! Steroids like dexamethasone are lifesavers here. They don't kill the cancer, but they quickly shrink the puffy swelling (edema) around the tumor, bringing relief fast.

question: Why does a drop in estrogen during menopause lead to atrophic vaginitis?

options.A: It permanently closes the internal cervical os.
options.B: It thins the vaginal lining and reduces natural moisture and elasticity.
options.C: It triggers an allergic reaction to normal vaginal secretions.
options.D: It encourages the massive overgrowth of anaerobic bacteria.

explanation: You got it! Lower estrogen levels make the vaginal walls thinner, drier, and more fragile, which easily leads to irritation and inflammation.

question: Which type of lubricant must you use during a pelvic exam if a Pap smear is planned?

options.A: Petroleum-based jelly
options.B: Water-soluble lubricant
options.C: Surgical mineral oil
options.D: Silicone-based oil

explanation: You got it! Petroleum or silicone jellies can mess up cellular lab samples like Pap smears. Always stick to water-soluble products.

question: Which part of the eye makes the watery fluid (aqueous humor)?

options.A: The ciliary body
options.B: The trabecular meshwork
options.C: Schlemm's canal
options.D: The cornea

explanation: Great job! The ciliary body acts like a little factory, constantly making aqueous humor to nourish the inside parts of the eye.

question: What is the best approach for a nurse educating a patient with functional hypothalamic amenorrhoea?

options.A: Focusing strictly on surgical options without mentioning lifestyle changes
options.B: Telling the patient to immediately stop all daily physical activities forever
options.C: Assuring the patient that missed periods have no impact on long-term bone health

explanation: Helping the patient understand how food, rest, and stress levels connect to their cycle is empowering and guides them toward healing.

question: What is the main goal of end-of-life care for a dying patient?

options.A: Providing comfort and maintaining dignity
options.B: Using all available machines to prolong life
options.C: Speeding up the dying process safely
options.D: Finding a cure for terminal illnesses

explanation: At the end of life, the focus shifts from curing the disease to making sure the patient is comfortable, free from pain, and treated with respect. You are helping them live their remaining days peacefully!

question: What is a key role of a nurse acting as a community champion for reproductive health?

options.A: Writing national health insurance budget laws
options.B: Replacing traditional village chiefs in council meetings

options.D: Educating and advocating outside hospital walls

question: Why does sudden, heavy bleeding (acute blood loss) often cause tachycardia?

options.A: Low blood pressure completely shuts off parasympathetic signals
options.B: Red blood cells speed up electrical conduction when counts drop
options.C: The body compensates for low blood volume by making the heart pump faster
options.D: Bleeding directly irritates the SA node with excess iron

explanation: When blood volume drops, your clever body tries to keep blood flowing to vital organs by speeding up the heart to make up for the lower volume.

question: Why do we usually need to treat everyone in a household if just one person has pinworms?

options.A: Healthy people absorb extra nutrition from the medication
options.B: Insurance companies require every family member to take pills
options.C: Pinworms spread easily among people living in close contact
options.D: The drug loses its potency if not shared by a group

explanation: You nailed it! Pinworm eggs pass around so easily on hands, sheets, and dust that everyone in the house will likely just pass it back and forth if not treated together.

question: Why can a brain abscess cause symptoms that look just like a brain tumor?

options.A: It acts as a mass that takes up space and increases pressure inside the skull.
options.B: It causes the hair on the scalp to fall out rapidly.
options.C: It replaces normal brain cells with cancer cells.
options.D: It changes the genetic makeup of surrounding neurons over time.

explanation: A pocket of pus inside the head takes up physical space, just like a tumor. This raises the pressure inside the skull (ICP) and presses on nearby brain areas.

question: Why is cancer staging so important after a patient receives a confirmed diagnosis?

options.A: It guides treatment decisions and helps determine the overall prognosis
options.B: It identifies the exact environmental toxin that caused the disease
options.C: It guarantees that the patient will achieve full remission
options.D: It completely replaces the need for any laboratory blood tests

explanation: You got it! Staging lets the team know how far the cancer has spread, which helps them choose the best treatment plan and understand what lies ahead.

question: Why is training in adolescent psychology helpful for nurses?

options.A: It guarantees higher government salaries
options.B: It allows nurses to prescribe adult psychiatric drugs
options.C: It replaces the need for physical examinations
options.D: It helps providers communicate effectively without personal biases

question: What is the main job of activated charcoal when given for something a patient swallowed?

options.A: To neutralize stomach acid and prevent internal bleeding
options.B: To bind toxins in the gut and prevent them from entering the blood
options.C: To coat the throat and protect it from corrosive chemicals
options.D: To cause immediate vomiting and empty the stomach contents

explanation: Activated charcoal acts like a tiny sponge in the stomach! It grabs onto the toxins so they pass safely out of the body instead of entering the bloodstream.

question: Which of these is NOT a result of losing subcutaneous fat in old age?

options.A: Higher vulnerability to pressure injuries over bony areas
options.B: Increased ability to tolerate high summer temperatures
options.C: Impaired ability to maintain normal body warmth
options.D: Reduced natural cushioning against physical bumps

question: How does the World Health Organization define an unsafe abortion?

question: What is the primary imaging test used to confirm and evaluate a suspected bone fracture?

question: Why should nurses avoid using vague words like 'normal' when charting physical assessments?

options.B: Patients have a legal right to erase that word from their records

question: What immediate emergency action should you take if the chest tube accidentally pulls loose from the drainage machine?

options.A: Submerge the end of the tubing in sterile water to maintain a seal

options.C: Wash the disconnected plastic ends with soap and tap water

question: Which cells swallow trapped fats inside artery walls to help form fatty streaks?

options.A: Platelets
options.B: Macrophages
options.C: Fibroblasts
options.D: Red blood cells

explanation: Macrophages are our immune cleanup cells, but when they eat too much trapped fat in the arteries, they turn into foam cells and start plaque buildup.

question: Why are prophylactic antibiotics usually given within one hour before the surgical incision is made?

options.A: To allow the surgical team time to perform hand scrubbing rituals
options.B: To neutralize any bacteria already present in the circulating air
options.C: To prevent the patient from experiencing nausea while on the operating table
options.D: To ensure peak tissue concentration of the drug when the skin is opened

explanation: Timing is everything! Giving the drug right before surgery means the antibiotic is fully active in the tissues the exact second the skin opens.

question: How does the high humidity inside a steam tent help a patient with a heavy cough?

options.A: It dilates the tiny air sacs in the lower lungs
options.B: It kills bacterial infections in the upper airway
options.C: It numbs the throat nerves to stop the cough reflex
options.D: It liquefies thick mucus so it is easier to clear

explanation: Spot on! Moisture acts like magic on sticky mucus, thinning it out so the patient can cough it up easily.

question: Why should children with viral infections like chickenpox or flu never be given aspirin?

options.A: It causes severe green discoloration of the teeth
options.B: It completely stops the heart from beating
options.C: It is linked to Reye's syndrome, a dangerous brain and liver condition
options.D: It has no effect on pediatric fevers

explanation: Aspirin during viral illnesses can trigger Reye's syndrome—a rare but severe condition affecting the brain and liver. Always choose paracetamol instead!

question: What is one of the most common workplace hazards for nurses during medication rounds?

options.A: Airborne tuberculosis transmission
options.B: Accidental needle-stick injuries
options.C: Developing chronic bone fractures
options.D: Sudden chemical skin burns

question: An endometrioma happens when which of the following occurs?

question: What must a nurse always do when a calculated safety box requirement results in a fractional number like 12.3 boxes?

options.D: Always round down to the nearest lower whole number.
